review: diagnostic-failure-controls-k150 findings R1, R2 and R3

classifications.fixture_defect: A demonstrated fixture mechanism, repaired, with controls.
classifications.runtime_defect: A demonstrated runtime mechanism, repaired, with controls.
classifications.bound_exhausted_cause_unknown: The retained receipts show a bound that ran out. The runtime or fixture failed closed. No control reproduces the historical stall or identifies its cause. Later passing samples do not explain the failure.
classifications.defect_demonstrated_attribution_unresolv: A real defect is demonstrated, but the historical receipts contradict the condition that the control reproduces.

observations: fork-authority-k121/candidate-full: test_worker_capture.py:112 waitpid 20.291 us after cutoff
cases.mechanism: The runtime admitted the stale reap before the cutoff. The test timestamped the later syscall entry.
cases.repair: test_worker_capture.py asserts admission time and retains execution time.
test_shutdown.py asserts admission time and retains execution time.

observations: fork-channel-k116/parent-full-1: blocking-2-deferred-reap probe 4.944 ms after cutoff
command-dispatch-k129/candidate-full-1: same node 215.5 us after cutoff
caller-cleanup-k145/candidate-v2-full: assert -9 == 0, PID TERM then PID KILL
cases.mechanism: The k145 peer ignored TERM until its child declared readiness. With no declaration, the k151 control reproduces return code -9 with PID KILL, but the peer then prints no child PID. Both historical runs printed the child PID: 34536 in k145 run 179b4702 and 16638 in k132 run fc704d02. The peer prints that PID only after it leaves its readiness loop. So readiness was reached before KILL, and the never-ready condition is not the historical cause. Late readiness followed by slow exit is possible but unproven.
cases.repair: Commit d5251d7 (k143) honours TERM before child readiness. That repairs the demonstrated defect, not an identified historical cause.
cases.child_cleanup: k151 red: 9 timed cases end absent by retained PID. 3 never-ready cases end unknown because no child identity was retained. Their case-path scans find no process naming the case path. Green: 12 of 12 absent.
cases.k151_change: R1 and R2: attribution unresolved, child audit tri-state

observations: readiness-wakes-k132/parent-full-2 [True]: run 067dc917, leader exit 167.8 ms after TERM
[False]: run bdbfc1a5, leader exit 158.3 ms after TERM, rc -9
cases.mechanism: The fixture must exit within the 150 ms TERM grace. Measured post-TERM exit is 33-50 ms, also under 3x CPU oversubscription. The historical stall is not reproduced and its cause is unidentified. Runtime receipts are correct.
cases.demonstrated: Controls measure 33-50 ms post-TERM exit, also at load 48. None reproduces the 158.3 ms and 167.8 ms exits.
cases.k151_change: R3: no control demonstrates that the miss was unavoidable

observations: k140 parent-full: 11 failures, KeyError 'after_term' or assert (False)
cases.mechanism: The worker wrote its witness file after TERM inside the runtime's 13.5 ms KILL window. Every failure left a partial late-created-shutdown-*.tmp file.
cases.repair: The worker records TERM state in an inherited anonymous mmap. The parent publishes the witness after capture.

observations: bootstrap-bounds-k106: 2 x 'worker did not prebuffer the identity'
cases.mechanism: The fixture waits 150 ms for worker progress. No runtime operation is involved. The cause of the stall is unidentified.
cases.k151_change: R3: no control demonstrates that the miss was unavoidable

observations: incremental-shutdown-k110/green-full run e0d6a3f2: table '30416 30416 ?E' 2.8 ms after observed leader exit, state unknown, termination_ok False
cases.mechanism: Kqueue reports ESRCH once proc_find fails, after the last thread ends but before SZOMB. So the runtime observes exit while ps still prints ?E (P_WEXIT, no thread state). The parser rejected ?E.
cases.repair: controller.py accepts ?-with-E and counts E members as non-executable.
cases.k151_change: Stale phrase corrected: ESRCH comes from proc_find failure, not from exit start

observations: k137 parent-full: disposal and expected interruption
cases.mechanism: A real ps helper ran past its capture deadline (about 128 ms). The runtime killed and reaped it and failed closed as unknown or permission_unknown. Measured ps latency never exceeds 62.1 ms in 340 group queries.
cases.demonstrated: The runtime killed and reaped each late ps helper and failed closed. The control's maximum ps latency is 62.1 ms in 340 queries, below the historical deadline.
cases.k151_change: R3: no control demonstrates that the miss was unavoidable

observations: termination-cutoff-k85/full-1: 4 x ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
cases.mechanism: TERM at 0.3 s arrived before the peer printed its child PID. The current fixture keeps that 0.3 s startup dependency. A startup stall reproduces the exact error on final inputs.
cases.demonstrated: A startup stall on final inputs reproduces the exact error, so the fixture depends on startup within 0.3 s. Why the historical startup stalled is unknown.
cases.k151_change: R3: no control demonstrates that the miss was unavoidable
